payload.summary: All three amendments verified against source code. Amendment 1 correctly identifies an undocumented trade-off at the pH clamp boundary. Amendment 2 correctly identifies a staleness footgun for total_tracked_ions_mg() callers (the nitrogen cycle code already acknowledges the issue locally, but total_tracked_ions_mg itself lacks a precondition comment). Amendment 3 identifies a real mass-conservation violation in the v3->v4 migration where reserve_g is fabricated from structural biomass, injecting free N/C mass into the budget.

votes.rationale: Verified. At line 290, pH is clamped via clamp_carbonate_ph, and at line 291-292 species are reprojected using the clamped pH. The existing comment (lines 288-289) explains idempotency but does not mention that alkalinity consistency (HCO3 + 2*CO3 vs input alkalinity) is sacrificed at clamp boundaries while DIC is conserved. This is a non-obvious trade-off that a future maintainer could easily misinterpret. A brief documentation comment is low-cost and high-value.

Verified. bicarbonate_mg_total is included in total_tracked_ions_mg() (water.rs:215) and is only updated by resolve_carbonate_state() (chemistry.rs:345). The nitrogen cycle (nitrogen_cycle.rs:350-351) modifies alkalinity without resolving, and even has a local comment acknowledging the stale window. But total_tracked_ions_mg() itself has no precondition comment warning callers about the cache dependency. Since this function feeds TDS and conductivity, any future caller reading it after an alkalinity mutation but before resolution would silently get stale data. A doc comment on the function itself is the right location for this invariant.

Verified. The v3->v4 migration (save.rs:331-340) computes reserve_g = biomass * LIVE_BIOMASS_ORGANIC_FRACTION and injects it into the animal state. reserve_g is documented as 'assimilated organic reserve' (retained feeding, not structural mass) at biology.rs:94-99. It is independently counted in N/C budgets (budget.rs:248, 333), spent by fund_live_shrimp_biomass for hatching/maturation (shrimp.rs:641-651), and exported on removal (engine.rs:403-407). Since v3 saves had no reserve concept, seeding it from biomass creates mass ex nihilo—inflating the budget and potentially enabling immediate reproduction. Leaving reserve_g at 0.0 (serde default) correctly preserves the pre-migration physical state; shrimp would then accumulate reserve naturally through feeding.
